rule: A measured absence of a significant effect, including measured ineffectiveness, is no_effect; refutes is reserved for explicit contradiction of a stated or expected claim.
review: All 34 source spans and surrounding full-body results/discussion reviewed against the user ruling on 2026-09-27; engineering annotation review, not independent expert adjudication. Historical context strings remain verbatim even when their old label rationale is superseded here.

rows.quote: Prochloraz was very effective at reducing the growth of isolate 620.
rows.rationale: Positive in-vitro growth inhibition of isolate 620 remains supports under the ruling; it is not a null or contradiction.

rows.quote: Metrafenone also significantly reduced the growth of isolate 620 but growth was less severely affected compared to prochloraz treated flasks.
rows.rationale: Positive in-vitro growth inhibition remains supports; weaker efficacy than prochloraz is not a measured null under the ruling.

rows.quote: Prochloraz significantly reduced the growth of isolate 1722 in flask cultures, similar to isolate 620.
rows.rationale: The significant reduction in isolate 1722 growth remains supports under the positive-finding branch of the ruling.

rows.quote: In crop trial 1, there was no significant difference between the bubble development in the untreated control plots and prochloraz, B. velezensis QST 713 or Kos treated plots inoculated at a rate of 1 × 106 conidia m−2.
rows.rationale: No significant crop-trial-1 bubble-development difference versus untreated plots is a measured null, hence no_effect under the ruling.

rows.quote: However, we found that deltamethrin + PB bait sprays were ineffective in the field.
rows.rationale: The field-treatment finding is measured ineffectiveness, so the ruling requires no_effect; the nearby cage and jar results concern different settings, not an explicit contradiction of this field claim.

rows.quote: Cyantraniliprole or PB alone did not significantly affect mortality.
rows.rationale: PB alone did not significantly affect bioassay mortality, a measured null that remains no_effect under the ruling.

rows.quote: At all time points after the start of the bioassay, mortality was higher in the cyantraniliprole + PB treatment than in the water control (t270 = 4.85; p < 0.001).
rows.rationale: The combined treatment increased mortality versus water, a positive finding that remains supports under the ruling.

rows.quote: The fresh weight of the R blackgrass plants treated only with PBO did not differ from that of the untreated (control) plants, while the application of PBO two hours before the herbicide treatments considerably increased the herbicidal effect of ACCase- and ALS-inhibitors against the R blackgrass population.
rows.rationale: PBO alone had no measured fresh-weight difference versus untreated plants, so no_effect remains correct without transferring combination effects.

rows.quote: The pre-emergence application of either prosulfocarb or the formulation of chlorotoluron + diflufenican, even at half their recommended field label rate, provided 97–98% fresh weight reduction in both R and S blackgrass populations.
rows.rationale: The pre-emergence treatment reduced fresh weight at the stated rate, a positive finding that remains supports under the ruling.

rows.quote: More specifically, the fresh weight (a) and tiller number (b) produced by winter wheat plants significantly decreased with increasing density of the R and S blackgrass populations, whereas significant differences between populations were observed only in fresh weight.

rows.quote: In contrast, indaziflam applied postemergence (95 or 190 g ha−1) exhibited inconsistent control, with control values ranging from near 0% to 90%, and was not statistically different from the non‐treated control or treatment with glufosinate (Fig. ).

rows.quote: Glufosinate (1680 g a.i. ha−1) was also ineffective, with control statistically similar to the non‐treated control because of new P. annua emergence.

rows.quote: Fluridone applied preemergence was ineffective across several accessions, with izr‐1, izr‐2, izr‐5, and izr‐8 showing > 50% survival.
